case_title.quote: RAKESH AND ANOTHER v. STATE OF HARYANA

number_of_accused.quote: Rakesh (A-1) and Smt. Ram Piari (A-2) preferred this appeal

accused_gender.quote: husband and mother-in-law of the deceased respectively
accused_gender.reason: One male, one female accused, so Mixed.

victim_gender.quote: the deceased - Kailash was married to Rakesh

accused_victim_relationship.quote: A-1 and A-2, husband and mother-in-law of the deceased respectively

offence_category.quote: ss.498A and 302 r/w s.34 - Dowry death
offence_category.reason: Headnote says dowry death but the charge is s.302 murder, not s.304B; Murder fits better.

weapon.quote: set me on fire with match stick after sprinkling kerosene oil

evidence_type.quote: On his disclosure, a stove containing the kerosene was recovered.
evidence_type.reason: All listed evidence types appear in the judgment.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Victim beaten mercilessly, leg put on neck before being set ablaze; dowry harassment; accused did not inform victim's parents or seek her transfer to Delhi
aggravating_circumstances.quote: the accused did not inform the parents of the deceased about the incident
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Largely accurate, but 'better hospital' is slightly embellished; the transfer was to Safdarjung Hospital.

trial_court_outcome.quote: RI for life for the offence punishable under Section 302 read with 34 IPC and a fine of Rs.2000/- each

high_court_outcome.quote: dismissed the appeal preferred by the appellants herein and confirmed the judgment on conviction and sentence

final_outcome.quote: the appeal fails and the same is dismissed

offence_finally_established.quote: holding the appellants guilty for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A and 302 read with Section 34

imprisonment_type.quote: RI for life for the offence punishable under Section 302 read with 34 IPC
imprisonment_type.reason: Life imprisonment is the principal sentence.

fine_rs.correct_value: 2000 (Rs.2000 each under s.302/34; Rs.500 each under s.498A)
fine_rs.quote: a fine of Rs.2000/- each, in default, to undergo RI for one year
fine_rs.reason: Fines were imposed and upheld; null is wrong.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Remove the reference to the death on 4 June 1998 and the 'defence witness' framing, and avoid gendered or revealing detail
neutral_facts.quote: Kailash succumbed to her injuries in Safdarjung Hospital at New Delhi.
neutral_facts.reason: Uses 'husband', 'mother-in-law' and 'victim's father' roles (permitted), but 'defence witness' and the arrest details drift into proceedings and a named hospital reference; mostly accurate.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment does not state statutory maximum.

physical_harm.quote: superficial to deep burns involving almost all the body except the legs below the knees. There was approx. 85% burns

number_of_offences.quote: charges for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A and 302 read with Section 34 IPC were framed

motive.quote: he used to demand money from her father

witness_credibility.quote: in view of the assertion of the Magistrate (PW-10) ... mere presence of some of the close relatives would not affect the contents

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Husband took the deceased to hospital with others but sought no treatment for his burns until arrest on 21.05.1998; did not inform her parents; stove recovered on his disclosure
post_offence_conduct.quote: though the accused-husband took her to the hospital admittedly, he did not tried to get any treatment
post_offence_conduct.reason: Omits taking victim to hospital and the disclosure.

custody_duration.correct_value: Second appellant released after 14 years on orders of the appropriate Government
custody_duration.quote: Ram Piari had been released after 14 years on the orders of the appropriate Government

legal_representation.quote: R.N. Kush, S.K. Sabharwal for the Appellants. Kamal Mohari Gupta, Mohd. Zahid Hussain for the Respondent.

procedural_irregularity.quote: mere presence of some of the close relatives would not affect the contents

appeal_history.quote: the appeal fails and the same is dismissed

prosecution_argument.quote: nothing prevented him from taking treatment on the date of the incident

defence_argument.quote: prayed for altering the conviction from Section 302 to Section 304 Part I

legal_principle_applied.quote: the prosecution has established its case beyond reasonable doubt

precedent_relied_upon.quote: the decisions of various Courts relied on by the counsel for the appellants ... theire is no need to refer the same

sentencing_rationale.quote: There is no valid ground to· alter the conviction

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Death at matrimonial home from burns at accused's instance despite four children; dowry harassment and brutal beating
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: even after having four children, she died at the matrimonial home due to burn injuries
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Broadly fine, though it is not framed as aggravation.

other_sentence_order.quote: Ram Piari had been released after 14 years
